chapter: The Los Angeles music scene in the early 1930s
title: The Spikes Brothers and getting to Huntington Park
summary: Blakeney says the Spikes brothers mattered for their songs and for hiring musicians; he worked with them in Huntington Park.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: There were two very important gentleman, it seemed, called the Spikes Brothers, Johnny and Reb. Why were they so important, Mr. Blakeney, during this time and previously to 1930; the Spike Brothers, why were they so important to the music scene, and particularly to the black musicians?
Because of the songs they wrote, like "Someday Sweetheart" and others which became very popular back in those days.
Did they get employment for other musicians, within their band? Did people come to them to hire other musicians?
Yes, they did. They worked out in Huntington Park, I guess, with their own group and hired other musicians
but I worked out there myself with him for a little while.
Did the Spikes Brothers ever have a club of their own?
No, not that I can remember.
Their primary role then was as orchestra leaders and as/com-songposers?
Many of the musicians at this time sort of gravitated around them is that correct?
Yes, it is, to an extent.

Huntington Park, the area that you just mentioned, was a long, long way away from the Twelfth and Central area. Approximately how much time can you recall, did it take, for you to get to a job? Considering that most of the musicians lived in the area of Ninth, Eleventh or
Twelfth Street. How long did it take for you to get to Huntington Park at that time? Oh, not long, twenty or thirty minutes.
I'm trying to think of some of the places we played. Other than Huntington Park, you're saying?
